newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia said seeking Taiwan uranium sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia said seeking Taiwan uranium sales.

text.p: The Australian government is looking at ways Australia could sell uranium to Taiwan to avoid present restrictions, Phillip Shirvington, chief executive of uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, said.
The lack of a government-to-government agreement between Australia and the Republic of China (Taiwan) had held up Australian uranium exports to Taiwan for some time, he said.
Taiwan had a strong nuclear programme and was interested in buying uranium from Australia, Shirvington told a uranium conference in Darwin on Tuesday.
The sale of uranium required a safeguards agreement between Australia and the receiving country, he said.

The two Chinas standoff between the mainland People's Republic of China and Taiwan meant the Australian government had to enter into a government-to-government agreement with the Republic of China for sales to take place, he said.

Taiwan had found a way of buying uranium from Canada through uranium from that country being made subject to U.S. safeguards, he said. He said the Australian government was investigating a similar procedure to sell uranium to Taiwan.
State utility Taiwan Power Co last month invited bids for up to 750,000 pounds (340,000 kg) of uranium a year to fuel its nuclear power plants.
Taiwan has three nuclear power plants which consume a total of 2.5 million pounds of uranium fuel rods a year.
Mainland China has consistently objected to the Australian government entering into any official agreements with Taiwan.
